key_insight: OSReward proposes a standardized way to evaluate reward models that judge computer-use agent trajectories across different platforms. The core idea is to make CUA assessment more consistent, scalable, and comparable by using VLM-based judges under a common evaluation framework.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of reliable, scalable verification for whether a computer-using agent actually completed a task as instructed. Human annotators and manually written verifiers do not scale well, while current VLM-based reward models are hard to compare fairly across platforms and tasks.
method: Defines a standardized evaluation framework for cross-platform computer-use reward models.
Uses trajectory-level assessment of agent actions, states, and reasoning to verify task success.
Positions vision-language models as automated judges and evaluates them under a unified benchmark-like setup.
impact: This helps researchers and practitioners compare reward models more fairly and measure progress in computer-use agents. It also supports better data curation and reinforcement learning by enabling scalable task verification.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing CUA trajectory -> reward model judge -> success/failure verdict
Cross-platform comparison chart illustrating performance consistency across environments
Icon set for actions, states, reasoning, and verification
Benchmark-style scorecard summarizing standardized evaluation metrics
paper_title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
paper_authors: Qiushi Sun, Kanzhi Cheng, Yian Wang, Bowen Yang, Hang Yan
